sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Establishment**: Founded in **1890** under the direction of Sir George King to survey the plant resources of the British Indian Empire.
• **Reorganization**: Restructured in **1954** as a primary research institution for systematic botany and floristic studies.
• **Mandate**: To document the **plant wealth** of India, conduct **taxonomic research**, and maintain **National Herbaria**.
• **Key Metric**: BSI is the nodal agency for the **Flora of India** project and provides scientific inputs for the **National Biodiversity Authority (NBA)**.

items.definition: The science of naming, describing, and classifying organisms. BSI focuses on plant taxonomy to identify species for conservation.
A repository of dried plant specimens used for reference and research. The Central National Herbarium (CNH) is the largest in Asia.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Flora of India Project**: A multi-volume series documenting the plant diversity of the country.
• **Red Data Book**: Assessment of threatened plant species to guide conservation policy.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Shortage of trained taxonomists, climate change-induced habitat loss, and invasive species.
• **Solutions**: Digitization of herbarium specimens and integration of DNA barcoding for species identification.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'BSI-H-1890' (BSI, Howrah, 1890).
• **Decoded Meaning**: BSI was established in 1890 and its main hub is in Howrah.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: BSI is NOT a regulatory body like the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA). It is a research and survey organization. Do not confuse its advisory role with the enforcement powers of the NBA.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Taxonomic Impediment' when discussing the lack of trained professionals in biodiversity conservation.

keyTakeaways: BSI is the apex research body for plant taxonomy under MoEFCC.
It maintains the Central National Herbarium in Howrah.
It provides the scientific backbone for the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
